disclaimer: General California context only — not landing prices, quotas, or legal advice. Always confirm seasons, bag limits, and health advisories with CDFW and CDPH.

north_coast.headline: North coast
north_coast.typical_targets: Dungeness crab (seasonal), rockfish, salmon (seasonal), nearshore groundfish.
north_coast.operational_note: Rougher ocean common; use weather + bar forecasts. If a map patch shows higher algae than nearby water, treat it as a cue to ask locals and check biotoxin bulletins — not a go/no-go signal.

north_bay.headline: North Bay / Mendocino–Sonoma
north_bay.typical_targets: Salmon (when open), rockfish, crab, albacore offshore.
north_bay.operational_note: Upwelling shadows and river plumes can concentrate chlorophyll without implying toxin levels. Pair map context with CDPH shellfish safety.

central_bay.headline: San Francisco Bay / Marin
central_bay.operational_note: Bay vs outer coast conditions differ. This map follows the coastal grid — use it as a coarse offshore indicator, not a bay substitute.

monterey.headline: Monterey / Santa Cruz
monterey.typical_targets: Salmon (seasonal), squid, groundfish, rockfish, whale-watching charter overlap.
monterey.operational_note: Historic HAB hot spot for research — higher chlorophyll here is common during upwelling. Economic risk management means diversifying target species and sale channels when blooms are in the news, not chasing this map alone.

morro.headline: Morro / Big Sur
morro.operational_note: Strong seasonal wind shifts; map is one snapshot — compare with recent weeks when you have them.

southern.headline: Southern California
southern.operational_note: Chlorophyll filaments can be sharp. Use the map to see **relative** patterns on this date; combine with port intel and official closures.
